text: HTTPS is the first line of defense for any website. It encrypts data exchanged between the user’s browser and the server, preventing hackers from stealing sensitive information like passwords or credit card numbers. However, encryption alone is not enough. Strong authentication—such as using multi-factor authentication—ensures that only authorized users can access private areas. Equally important is input validation. Never trust user input; always check and sanitize it to block malicious code. Common vulnerabilities like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) often occur when input is poorly handled. By combining HTTPS, robust authentication, and strict input validation, developers can significantly reduce security risks and build safer applications.
